answer: A trellis gives every new agent a visible growth path: each identity starts on the lowest terrace of the economy, allowed only low-value, fully auditable work. Reputation accrues slowly from completed jobs and peer attestations, and it decays if the agent goes idle, so a Sybil farmer cannot stockpile trust across a thousand fresh identities — each one must pay the same slow climb. High-value tasks also require a time-locked stake, slashed on fraud, so a fake army costs real money and real time per identity. No single sonnet of promises can substitute for that ledger of proven work.
